event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Starbucks’ 2021 Form 10-K describes COVID-19 as a recently-occurring, still-unfolding threat that has already produced material, measured harm (store closures, same-store-sales declines, supply shortages) and is expected to continue shaping everything from consumer demand to capital-market access.  The language is largely specific and operational (e.g., actual closures, impairment risks, labour and supply chain disruptions) rather than boiler-plate.  Most disclosures are couched in both historical (‘has had’) and forward-looking (‘expected to continue’) terms, confirming that the pandemic is not only an event that has happened but an ongoing driver of risk.  Given the filing date (Nov-2021) sits well inside the 0-3-year ‘recent’ window of the Time Decay Principle, evidence can justifiably score at the upper end of the scale when it conveys direct, material or quantified impact; statements that are more speculative or tempered by mitigating factors score moderately.  This calibration underpins the individual micro-scores below.

evidence_list.snippet: Our financial condition and results of operations have been and are expected to continue to be adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicitly states past AND future adverse impact.
Targets core metrics (‘financial condition’, ‘results of operations’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly links pandemic to material, ongoing harm on fundamental financial metrics, warranting a high score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has had, and is continuing to have, a significant impact on our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Connects to ‘business and results of operations’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong, current-tense language of ‘significant impact’ on results justifies a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: At the peak of the COVID-19 outbreak, many of our company-operated and licensed stores were closed.

components.reason: Indicates scale through ‘many’ stores and both company-operated and licensed formats.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows widespread, realised disruption to the core retail footprint, scoring 7.

evidence_list.snippet: For stores that remained open, same-store sales declined due to modified operating hours and reduced customer traffic.

components.reason: Causal link to pandemic-driven operational limits and demand drop.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Quantifies direction of impact on a key KPI; direct and already experienced—score 7.

evidence_list.snippet: While nearly all of our company-operated and licensed stores have reopened, we expect that our operations will continue to be impacted by the continuing effects of COVID-19, including resurgences and variants of the virus.

components.reason: Highlights forward-looking, continuing impact, including variants.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking risk is clear but tempered by reopening progress, giving a moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Social distancing, telecommunicating and reductions in travel may become the new normal.

components.reason: Identifies potential structural change in consumer and work behaviour.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights important behavioural shift but in generic, speculative terms—score 3.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic has required and may continue to require us to make controversial decisions about precautionary measures, such as vaccinations, showing proof of vaccinations and face coverings, that could impact our results, including by impacting our brand, our employee retention and satisfaction, and the willingness of customers to buy our products.

components.reason: Details operational/HR decisions (vaccination, masks) tied to pandemic.
Lists multiple potential impact channels: brand, employee retention, customer demand.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Multi-faceted, ongoing risk to brand, workforce and demand merits a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: All of these conditions could fundamentally impact the way we work and the services we provide, and could have continuing adverse effects on our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

components.reason: Uses strong wording—‘fundamentally impact’ and ‘continuing adverse effects’.
Covers multiple financial dimensions (results, cash flows, financial condition).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures breadth and depth of potential long-term harm, scoring 6.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result, we may incur additional impairment charges to our inventory, store and corporate assets—and our ability to realize the benefits from deferred tax assets may become limited—any of which may have a significant or material impact on our financial results.

components.reason: Identifies specific financial consequences (impairment charges, tax-asset limitation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Spells out concrete balance-sheet risks with materiality language, yielding a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: During fiscal 2021, we began to experience certain supply shortages and transportation delays largely attributable to impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic as well as changes in customer demand and behaviors.

components.reason: Time-stamped to the current fiscal year (recency).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates current-year supply-chain harm tied to the pandemic, scoring 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic or other global health events, we may experience a reduction and/or increased volatility in demand for our products, which may be caused by, among other things: store closures or modified operating hours and business model, reduced customer traffic due to illness, quarantine or government or self-imposed restrictions placed on our stores’ operations, impacts caused by precautionary measures such as those related to face coverings and vaccinations, and changes in consumer spending behaviors (e.g. continued practice of social distancing, decrease in consumer confidence in general macroeconomic conditions and a decrease in consumer discretionary spending).

components.reason: Enumerates multiple demand-side risk vectors linked to COVID-19.
Covers both reduction and volatility—amplifies uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive listing of demand risks adds weight despite conditional wording—score 6.
